title: A Six-Parameter Cosmology with Fixed Matter and Baryon Fractions
content: Can a geometric allocation of matter account for the microwave sky and galaxy distances as well as a model that fits those amounts independently? We fix the present total matter and baryon fractions at \( \Omega_m=1/\pi \) and \( \Omega_b=1/(2\pi^2) \) and use the two available parameter positions to describe a variable effective stress. The resulting model has six adjustable cosmological quantities, matching the conventional flat cosmological-constant plus cold-dark-matter model (ΛCDM). Against Planck cosmic microwave background measurements and DESI galaxy-distance data, its fitted score is lower by 4.794. Allowing both densities to vary within the same stress family improves the score by a further 2.266 with two additional coordinates. Jointly refitting Pantheon+ supernova distances retains an equal-count advantage of 3.656. A separate matched neutrino-and-helium sensitivity test gives an advantage of $6.298$ for the microwave-background-plus-galaxy comparison. Toroidal Scale Mechanics motivates the fixed fractions through its geometric allocation of substrate response and interprets the fitted stress history as a candidate projection of scale-dependent tension. A conserved material action supplies the pressureless-plus-constant-tension background; the variable extension is tested with conventional cosmological transfer equations and a specified perturbation treatment. The results identify quantitative targets for deriving the fraction selection, variable stress, and optical readout from the substrate's common dynamics.
